interest: Shows Yokohama Specie Bank's wartime liquidation rippling through Latin American trade claims and bondholder proof-of-claim procedures.
keywords: Superintendent of Banks of the State of New York
Banco de la Provincia de Buenos Aires
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.51611, covering January 1941 through December 1944) documents the extraterritorial, domestic legal, financial, and diplomatic ramifications of the closure and liquidation of Japanese banking branches in the United States—primarily the New York agency of the Yokohama Specie Bank, Ltd.—following the outbreak of the Pacific War. Key issues addressed include the division of authority between state regulators (the Superintendent of Banks of the State of New York) and federal wartime agencies (the Alien Property Custodian and the Treasury Department's Foreign Funds Control), diplomatic inquiries from the Dominican Republic regarding the collection of pre-war commercial drafts drawn by Osaka firm Sanko & Co., cross-border financial tracing involving the Banco de la Provincia de Buenos Aires and Banco do Brasil in Argentina, instructions to bondholders regarding claims on Japanese dollar bonds, and pre-war intelligence coordination between the FBI, State Department, and Treasury concerning Japanese banking operations.

subfiles.about: Notice informing holders of Japanese dollar bonds that the New York branch of the Yokohama Specie Bank is being liquidated and enclosing claim forms.

subfiles.about: Letter detailing the legal and supervisory basis for the New York Superintendent's liquidation of the Yokohama Specie Bank.
